_comment: THE NINE EXISTING STAGING RECEIPTS, PINNED.
private.staging_install_receipts on the verified staging backend holds nine
rows through Stage 09. The installer compares the live ledger against this
file EXACTLY — every stage name, every sha256, and the order they were
installed in — and refuses the whole stage on any difference.
That comparison is also what binds the installation to the right database.
A hostname proves nothing (a tunnel or a copied connection string looks
identical); nine matching receipts are an identity the wrong database
cannot produce.
THIS FILE SHIPS UNPOPULATED ON PURPOSE. The nine values were read by Codex
during verification and were NOT included in the correction brief, so they
are not known here. They are not guessed: inventing a stage name or a
checksum would make the comparison pass against a ledger nobody checked,
which is worse than having no comparison at all.
TO POPULATE — one read-only query against staging, then paste the result:
SELECT jsonb_pretty(jsonb_build_object(
'status','VERIFIED',
'database', current_database(),
'captured_at', now(),
'receipts', (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
'ordinal', ord, 'stage', stage, 'sha256', sha256)
ORDER BY ord)
FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY installed_at, stage) AS ord,
stage, sha256
FROM private.staging_install_receipts) r)));
Or let seal-manifest.sh do it, which runs exactly that query and then
validates its own output:
bash scripts/esign-staging/seal-manifest.sh capture "<staging connection>"
bash scripts/esign-staging/seal-manifest.sh validate
Paste the three fields into this file, keep the ordinals as the query
returned them, and have the result reviewed before the installer is run.
While status is UNPOPULATED the installer stops before it opens a
transaction.
